question: A 2D echocardiogram with Doppler is the single most important investigation for classifying heart failure by ejection fraction and identifying its aetiology, and should be performed in all patients with suspected heart failure.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. ESC/AHA/ACC guidelines recommend echocardiography in all patients with suspected heart failure. It is the cornerstone investigation: the only modality that simultaneously measures LVEF, identifies structural causes (valvular, regional wall motion), and estimates haemodynamics.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Echocardiography directly measures LVEF (classifying HFrEF/HFmrEF/HFpEF), assesses regional wall motion (ischaemic aetiology), evaluates valvular structure and function, measures right ventricular function, and estimates pulmonary artery pressure. No other single investigation provides this breadth of information.
